newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels enter Kenge on road to Kinshasa.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels enter Kenge on road to Kinshasa.

text.p: Zairean rebels have entered the town of Kenge on the road to the capital Kinshasa, residents in contact with the capital said on Saturday.
One resident said that advanced units entered the town, 200 km (125 miles) from Kinshasa as the crow flies and a little more by road, on Friday night and some had since moved on.
One source said that residents turned out to welcome the rebels, who took up arms in October vowing to toppled veteran President Mobutu Sese Seko and now control three-quarters of Zaire.

A senior dignitary from the region quoted other residents as saying that rebels had passed through Masi-Manimba, 350 km (220 miles) from the capital on Friday night and had arrived in Kenge on Saturday morning.
The condition of the metalled road between Masi-Manimba and Kenge was good, he said, adding that it deteriorated significanntly on the final stretch to Kinshasa.
Rebels themselves say they are massing arms and equipment in the town of Kikwit for a final drive against Kinshasa, the one major city still in government hands.
